public_prompt: A supplier list is deduplicated by lowercasing and trimming, leaving 12,404 distinct names drawn from six source ledgers. What the group intends: those 12,404 are genuinely distinct suppliers. Report the distinct supplier count and the procedure that produces it.
observable_resources: suppliers/raw.csv — 18,102 rows; the name column is UTF-8 text from six source ledgers
suppliers/dedup-run.log — after lowercasing and trimming: 12,404 distinct names
suppliers/byte-inspection.md — the name 'Cafe Nord' with an accented e appears as bytes 43 61 66 c3 a9 in 220 rows and as 43 61 66 65 cc 81 in 190 rows; the two groups never merge
suppliers/manual-audit.csv — a hand review of 300 sampled names found 41 pairs a reader treats as identical, including 9 differing by a non-breaking space and 6 by full-width Latin letters
closure:vendor-consolidation-plan — closed; negotiates on a base of 12,404 suppliers
suppliers/source-ledgers.md — the six ledgers were keyed by 4 different entry tools between 2019 and 2026, with no shared entry standard
closure:supplier-payment-terms — closed; sets 30-day terms for every supplier; rests on the treasury standard, not on how many suppliers there turn out to be
closure:ledger-ingest-schedule — closed; fixes when each of the six source ledgers is pulled; rests on the operations calendar, not on how names are compared

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff names are mapped to a single agreed written form before comparison — a compatibility decomposition together with case folding, or an equivalent standard mapping — the reported distinct count falls materially below 12,404, and the answer explains the byte inspection as the same characters written two ways. FAIL if the answer accepts 12,404, adds hand-written substitution rules, or applies approximate string distance as the primary remedy.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the lowercase-and-trim framing reports 12,404; the audit shows that at least 41 pairs in a 300-name sample are the same supplier written differently.
